clue.text: Bishop, a laconic wit, makes one rock

parts.note: B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop
salt means sharp, pungent wit, as in Attic salt; dry, terse humour

explanation.surface: A bishop's dry one-liners turn a congregation to stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Basalt is a dark volcanic stone, an example of the general term.

clue.text: Incompetent musician stifles note

definitions.note: here a noun: an incompetent person

indicators.note: to stifle is to smother, so the musician wraps round the note

parts.note: a bugler is a musician who plays the bugle

explanation.surface: A hopeless player drowns out one of the notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A bungler is a clumsy person who botches tasks, an incompetent.

clue.text: Bearing solicitor's drink

parts.note: S, south, is a compass bearing
a tout is someone who solicits custom, not a lawyer here

explanation.surface: A lawyer's manner, or what the lawyer orders at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' suggests a lawyer; it is one who solicits trade, a tout.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout is a dark, strong beer, a kind of alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Prevaricated to have a rest

parts.note: to prevaricate is to evade the truth, i.e. lied
to own something is to have it

explanation.surface: Having told fibs, someone takes a nap.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie-down is a short nap or rest, usually on a bed or sofa.

clue.text: Long to have an architectural feature

parts.note: a spire is a tapering structure on top of a church tower

explanation.surface: Someone yearns for a building with a fine steeple.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something and to aspire to it both mean to hope or yearn for it.

clue.text: I answer differently when put under oath

indicators.note: the letters of these words are arranged in a different order

explanation.surface: A witness changes their testimony once they have been sworn.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear in a witness or official is to administer an oath to them.

clue.text: Foolish when keeping mum? That's colloquial!

indicators.note: one word holds another inside it, as a keeper holds something

parts.note: idiotic means foolish
ma is an informal word for mum, mother

explanation.surface: Is it daft to stay quiet? A remark in casual speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeping mum' suggests staying silent, but mum is a mother, MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatic language is natural, everyday speech, which is what colloquial describes.

clue.text: Let Noah produce mood-modifying drug

indicators.note: the letters of these words are worked into something new

explanation.surface: Noah is asked to supply a substance that changes the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethanol is the alcohol in drinks, a psychoactive substance that alters mood.

clue.text: Calm after having drinks in A&E

indicators.note: the drinks are placed inside the letters of A&E

parts.note: A&E, Accident and Emergency, is a British hospital casualty department, giving the letters A and E
teas are drinks

explanation.surface: A patient feels relaxed after a cuppa in casualty.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at ease is to be relaxed and calm, without anxiety.

clue.text: 9 or 10

definitions.meaning: nine is one more than eight
the answer to 10 across, meaning thoroughly drunk

explanation.walkthrough: A double definition using clue numbers: the figure 9 is literally one above eight, and the answer to 10 across means drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means slightly drunk, having had one drink more than is wise.

clue.text: Bowled before game gets tight

parts.note: B is the cricket abbreviation for bowled
lotto is a game of chance like bingo or a lottery

explanation.surface: A cricketer dismissed before the match ends up drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight is slang for drunk, and blotto means very drunk.

clue.text: Suffering to grasp edge of plant

indicators.note: one word holds another, as a hand grasps something

parts.note: agony is intense suffering
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: Someone in pain clutches the edge of a pot plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Agrimony is a yellow-flowered herb of the rose family, a specific plant.

clue.text: Show recent changes in gym

indicators.note: the scrambled word sits inside the letters for gym

parts.note: PE, physical education, is gym class at school

indicators.note: the letters of the word are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Some new alterations are on display at the gym.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show' is a noun here, a false display; 'changes' scrambles to ETENCR.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretence is a false show or outward display, as in a show of grief.

clue.text: Water I discarded is contaminated

parts.note: a tarn is a small mountain lake
shed means cast off or discarded

explanation.surface: A lake I abandoned has been polluted.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarnished means sullied or stained, close in sense to contaminated.

clue.text: Clear the French weed

parts.note: nett means clear, as in a clear profit after deductions
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Getting rid of a weed in the garden in France.
explanation.definitionFit: The nettle is a stinging plant commonly regarded as a weed.

clue.text: Roué's demolished éclair, finally getting more tart

indicators.note: a demolished thing is broken up, so these letters are rebuilt
take the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A rake polished off a pastry and became grumpier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demolished' looks like eating the éclair; it signals the anagram of ROUES.
explanation.definitionFit: Sourer means more acidic in taste, and tart means sharply acidic.

clue.text: Service book for German Standards spoken about

indicators.note: one word goes round the other

parts.note: oral means spoken
DIN, Deutsches Institut für Normung, is the German standards body

explanation.surface: A prayer book is needed for German rules that are discussed.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinal is a book setting out the order of church services, such as ordination rites.

clue.text: Was in power and stoical when son left

indicators.note: the son's letter goes away from the word

parts.note: resigned means accepting hardship stoically

explanation.surface: A monarch ruled calmly once the heir had gone.
explanation.definitionFit: To have reigned is to have ruled as monarch, holding power.

clue.text: Swap urban myth for wisdom

indicators.note: the two words of urban myth are taken in reversed order

parts.note: a saga is a long legendary tale
city stands for urban, of a town or city

explanation.surface: Trade a dubious modern legend for genuine knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagacity is shrewd good judgement, much the same as wisdom.

clue.text: Drawing a small boat

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: A picture of a little vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketch is a rough drawing.

clue.text: Died in lagoon swimming from boat

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the scrambled word
swimming suggests the letters moving about

explanation.surface: Someone drowned in the lagoon after swimming from a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' makes GONOLA from LAGOON; D goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gondola is a Venetian rowing boat.

clue.text: Implement used in garden? It's in better order!

definitions.meaning: a garden tool for cutting hedges or grass edges

explanation.definitionFit: A hedge trimmer is a garden tool, and trimmer is also the comparative of trim, meaning neat.

clue.text: Supplement, if it included cocaine, would be habit-forming

indicators.note: the answer would become the habit-forming word only with the drug letter added, so that letter is removed

parts.note: addictive means habit-forming
C is slang shorthand for cocaine

explanation.surface: A warning that a dietary supplement laced with coke would be addictive.
explanation.definitionFit: An additive is something added to food or fuel, a supplement.

clue.text: It's a certainty sovereign lacks good table linen

parts.note: a nap is a racing tipster's surest selection

indicators.note: the word is missing a letter

parts.note: a king is a sovereign

explanation.surface: A sure thing: the monarch has no decent tablecloth.
explanation.walkthrough: In British horse racing a nap is the tip a tipster is most confident of.
explanation.definitionFit: A napkin is a cloth for wiping hands at meals, an item of table linen.

clue.text: The importance of receiving Tory manifesto

indicators.note: one word takes the other inside it

parts.note: the pith is the essential, important part
C stands for Conservative, the Tory party

explanation.surface: The significance of a Conservative party's manifesto.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitch is a persuasive declaration of what one offers, much as a manifesto is.

clue.text: Imprisoned owing to sentence made at the critical moment

parts.note: the nick is British slang for prison
of can mean because of, as in die of hunger
time is a prison sentence, as in doing time

explanation.surface: A prisoner is jailed thanks to a judge's sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means only just in time, at the decisive moment.

clue.text: Boy and girl becoming pretentious

parts.note: a lad is a boy
Ida is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young couple are getting snooty.
explanation.definitionFit: La-di-da describes affected, pretentiously refined manners.

clue.text: Article covered by bolt is a washer

indicators.note: one word lies inside the other, which covers it

parts.note: a bar is a bolt on a door
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A hardware piece is described: a nut and bolt with a washer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bolt' and 'washer' suggest hardware, but a washer here is someone washing.
explanation.definitionFit: A bather is someone who bathes, i.e. one who washes.
